messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: Smart-routing error spike detected for tenant=acme-marketing. 5xx on fallback path, cross-region retries >50% in 2m. Severity: P1. Paging oncall-sre. (alert_id=sr-fallback-1965554321)

devon: oncall here, looking. noticing a spike in routing decisions from hosted->dedicated that keep getting rejected and then retried back into hosted.

alyssa: same, grafana shows policy-evaluator loop: policy A -> fallback to region eu-west -> fallback to region us-east -> back to hosted pool which is full -> repeat. latency and token errors for requests.

jordan: are we sure this is a policy config change? any recent rollout?

maria: I rolled out a minor update to the capacity-tier routing weights ~14m ago (PR #4221) to reduce dedicated pool usage. Could that interact?

devon: possible. can you link the rollout? we might need to revert or pin affected tenant.

maria: https://git.internal/r/4221 — it touched policy priority scoring and a fallback weight param.

kai-eng: seeing logs from the runtime: repeated request hops with error "incompatible-model-variant" when moving hosted->dedicated. Looks like the dedicated pool doesn't have the requested quantized variant so the runtime rejects and sends back failure to routing, which triggers fallback to hosted, which then again routes into dedicated due to weight changes -> loop.

devon: ok that explains the wrong-model-variant piece. so routing policy is aggressively pushing to dedicated but dedicated can't serve that variant for tenant's model. result: retries and capacity churn.

sam-cs: customer impact? Any affected accounts we should notify now?

alyssa: acme-marketing visible errors in logs; ~2.1k requests failed in last 10m, 40% latency increase. We should mark as partial outage for them.

sam-cs: notifying account team + sending provisional status update.

devon: mitigation plan: 1) disable automatic fallback from hosted->dedicated for tenant acme-marketing (circuit-breaker) 2) revert the routing weight change 3) TTL pin their requests to hosted variant until we fix variant availability in dedicated. We'll do 1 then 3, minimal impact.

jordan: who has console ops permission to change per-tenant routing? I can if needed.

maria: I can revert PR but that's riskier. prefer targeted override.

kai-eng: I can add a temporary policy in the control plane: `policy.override(tenant=acme-marketing, allow_dedicated=false, reason="incident-1965554321")`

devon: do it. post the API call here. include TTL.

kai-eng: running now: ```http
POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/policies/overrides
{"tenant":"acme-marketing","allow_dedicated":false,"expires_in":"30m","note":"temp isolate due to incompatible-variant loop"}
```

kai-eng: response 200, override-id=ovr-1965554321. Routing logs show immediate drop in hosted->dedicated attempts for that tenant.

alyssa: errors for acme dropped from 5xx to nominal within 45s. latency back to baseline. great work.

devon: step 2: lower risk revert not needed now. we'll keep override for 30m and start a safe rollout to fix dedicated pool variant list. who owns artifact publish to dedicated?

maria: ops-team handles model variant packaging. I'll coordinate publishing the missing quantized variant to the dedicated pool for that model id: model-white-2025-q4. ETA 20m.

jordan: in parallel, I'm going to add a circuit-breaker improvement ticket so future policy scoring respects variant availability before weighting dedicated higher. I'll create an RFC and link.

devon: logging note: record incident tags: cause=policy-weight-change, symptom=variant-mismatch-loop, mitigation=per-tenant-override, customer-impact=acme-marketing partial outage.

sam-cs: sent customer note: "We've isolated your traffic to hosted to maintain availability; engineers are publishing a compatible variant into dedicated. We'll follow up after fix."

kai-eng: push to dedicated pool: ```
# artifact publish
upload model-white-2025-q4-INT8.tar.gz -> dedicated-pool-us-east
verify checksum: ok
activate variant: model-white-2025-q4-int8
```

kai-eng: activation complete, health checks green.

maria: once variant active, we should remove override and let normal routing resume with a cautious ramp.

devon: rolling back override now. ```http
DELETE https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/policies/overrides/ovr-1965554321
```

devon: response 200. traffic starts hitting dedicated but we need to watch for errors.

alyssa: first 5m after re-enable: no incompatible-model-variant errors for acme. error rate stable.

jordan: adding gradual weight ramp in runtime: from 0%->50% over 10m for this tenant to avoid shock. Pushing change.

kai-eng: weight ramping applied. monitoring.

sam-cs: customer updated: "Variant available in dedicated; resuming normal routing under controlled ramp. We'll monitor and confirm."

devon: closing mitigation. Post-incident actions: - IR doc (owner: devon) - postmortem with root cause analysis (owner: jordan) - enforce pre-check in policy deploy pipeline for variant availability (owner: maria) - automated tenant-level circuit-breakers for model-variant mismatch (owner: kai-eng)

maria: posting a retrospective FR to RFC repo and linking PR for pipeline checks.

devon: thanks everyone. tagging incident resolved for now, will keep thread open for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident sr-fallback-1965554321 acknowledged by devon, status=mitigated, duration=00:34:08, responders=[devon, kai-eng, maria, alyssa, jordan, sam-cs]."
